intended_object: An auxiliary cocone on the diagram i ↦ Hom(F_i, S) (with maps given by precomposition), whose apex is the set of continuous maps c.pt → S. It sends a stage map g : F_i → S to the composite c.pt → F_i → S. The docstring and the module's goal (comparing colim_i Hom(F_i, S) with Hom(lim F, S)) say what it is for.
explanation:
The definition is a proof device. It packages the canonical maps Hom(F_i, S) → Hom(c.pt, S), g ↦ π_i ≫ g, as a cocone. Its only purpose is to induce the comparison map from the filtered colimit of stage-hom sets to maps out of the cone point; the module later shows this map is a bijection when the cone is limiting. On its own, a cocone like this is not a standard mathematical notion that needs a definition: it is the image of the cone under the hom functor (–, S), restated in this specific setting.

The construction itself is correct:
- The component at op i is g ↦ c.π.app i ≫ toProfinite.map g.
- Naturality follows from functoriality of `toProfinite` together with the cone condition `c.w`.

As the docstring says, no limiting hypothesis is needed. Mathlib has no named declaration for this specific cocone.
